newsitem.title: CHINA: China says time not ripe for talks with Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China says time not ripe for talks with Taiwan.

text.p: Conditions are not yet right for a resumption of stalled talks between Beijing and its island rival Taiwan, Chinese state media on Wednesday quoted a senior official as saying.

Taipei had not accepted the principle of a unified China, a precondition for talks with the mainland, said Tang Shubei, executive vice-chairman of the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits.
"Conditions, including the political atmosphere, are not ripe for a resumption of talks," the China Daily quoted Tang as saying.
Association President Wang Daohan was ready to meet Koo Chen-fu, head of Taiwan's Straits Exchange Foundation, but only if Taipei accepted the principle of "One China", Tang said.
Political talks between the two sides, rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, have been stalled since a 1995 visit by Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui to the United States.
China, which considers Taiwan a rebel province and threatens to invade if it declares formal independence, has long tried to isolate the island diplomatically and was enraged by the Lee visit.
Taiwan has denied it is seeking independence but says reunification with the rest of China will only be possible when the mainland introduces democracy to its political system.

Beijing did not oppose Taipei's efforts to develop economic and cultural ties with other countries, but opposed all actions aimed at creating "Two Chinas" or "One China, One Taiwan", the Xinhua news agency quoted Tang as saying.
